# pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server Gotify notification endpoint: a [Gotify](https://gotify.net) server PBS pushes notifications to, as messages of one application. A notification reaches an endpoint only through a matcher: route notifications to this one with a `pbs_notification_matcher` whose `target` names it.

PBS does not contact the server when it saves the endpoint; a wrong setting shows when PBS sends the first notification, or at once with `send_test_on_apply`. PBS reaches the server through the HTTP proxy in the node's settings, when one is set.

~> **PBS refuses to delete an endpoint a matcher targets.** When a change of `name` replaces an endpoint that a `pbs_notification_matcher` targets, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` on the endpoint, so that the matcher moves to the new endpoint before the old one goes.

Endpoint and matcher names share one namespace. Managing notification endpoints needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`, reading them `Sys.Audit on /system/notifications`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Push notifications to a Gotify server, as messages of one of its
# applications, and route errors there.
resource "pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify" "phones" {
  name    = "gotify"
  server  = "https://gotify.example.com"
  comment = "The admins' phones"

  # The application token is write-only: it never reaches the plan or state,
  # and PBS receives it when the endpoint is created and whenever
  # token_wo_version changes.
  token_wo         = var.gotify_token
  token_wo_version = 1

  # PBS does not contact the server when it saves the endpoint; a test
  # message on every apply that creates or changes it does.
  send_test_on_apply = true
}

variable "gotify_token" {
  description = "Token of the Gotify application PBS sends as."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}

resource "pbs_notification_matcher" "errors_to_phones" {
  name           = "errors-to-gotify"
  target         = [pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify.phones.name]
  match_severity = ["error"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, 2 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Matchers name it in `target`. Changing it replaces the endpoint.
- `server` (String) Base URL of the Gotify server, such as `https://gotify.example.com`, without a trailing slash: PBS posts the messages to `<server>/message`.
- `token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Application token PBS sends the messages with, created in Gotify under Apps. Write-only: Terraform passes it to PBS without storing it in the plan or state, and PBS never returns it, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives it when the object is created and whenever `token_wo_version` changes. Requires `token_wo_version`, and Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later.
- `token_wo_version` (Number) Version of `token_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `token_wo`.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `disable` (Boolean) Whether the endpoint is disabled: matchers that target it send nothing through it. Defaults to `false`.
- `send_test_on_apply` (Boolean) Have PBS send a test notification through the endpoint after every apply that creates or changes it, unless it is disabled, so that a wrong setting fails the apply instead of going unnoticed until a real notification is lost. Defaults to `false`. It exists only in Terraform: turning it on changes nothing in PBS and sends nothing by itself, and every test delivers a real message. PBS waits up to 10 seconds for the Gotify server to take the message. A failed test fails the apply. When the test after a create fails, the provider deletes the endpoint again, so the next apply creates and tests it again — should that delete fail too, the endpoint is kept and marked tainted; when the test after an update fails, the endpoint keeps the change, and the next apply tests again only if the endpoint changes again. Sending a test needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `name`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.
- `origin` (String) Where the endpoint comes from: `user-created` for every Gotify endpoint, as PBS has no built-in one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify.phones
  identity = {
    name = "gotify"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, such as `gotify`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify.phones
  id = "gotify"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Gotify endpoints are imported by name. PBS never returns the token, so
# token_wo_version is empty after an import, and the next apply sends
# token_wo, replacing the token PBS has.
terraform import pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify.phones gotify
```
